one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-01 (last trading day Fri 2026-10-30) very likely includes FormFactor's Q3 2026 report: Q2 was reported 2026-07-29 and the quarter ended 2026-09-26, so a late-October print (~Oct 28-29, date not yet announced) is the base case. Guide was $270M +/- $10M revenue and $0.86 +/- $0.09 non-GAAP EPS, with management calling out Foundry & Logic strength; FORM beat the top end of its range in Q1 and Q2 and the new Nvidia/TSMC GPU probe-card second-source role (Deutsche Bank, 2026-09-30) starts in H2 2026, so a beat is more likely than not, but the stock has just rallied ~10% on a sell-side initiation (no company 8-K filed that day) and trades ~40x my 2027E EPS, so a good-not-great Q4 guide could still produce a drop (it fell after a record Q1). Peer SK hynix Q3 results (late Oct) are a read-across. Momentum after the jump vs. reversal roughly offset; I centre the distribution at ~$148.5 (between the brief's $147.90 and the $149.15 close the caller reported) with ~20% one-month log-vol (85% annual / 3.5 is ~24%, trimmed slightly because part of realized vol came from earlier gap moves), i.e. a near-symmetric spread with fat enough tails for an earnings gap of +/-15%.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (2028E non-GAAP EPS $4.40 x 32x + $4.20/sh net cash = $145, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (2027E FCF/share $3.80 / 2.75% = $138, weight 0.4) gives ~$142 fair value 12 months out, slightly below the $147.90 last close.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026E ~ $3.20 (0.56+0.82+0.86+~0.95). 2027E ~ $3.90 (+22%: HBM4 16-high test intensity, Nvidia GPU second-source ramp per DB, Technoprobe peer growing 40%+). 2028E ~ $4.40 (+13%, slowing as memory capex normalizes); close to the SA contributor's 2028E $4.25.

SA contributor uses 40x and DB's $200 target implies more; Technoprobe's 25% drawdown on 'end of AI capex acceleration' (Jul-2026) shows how fast the multiple compresses. 32x on two-year-forward EPS reflects a premium semicap name late in an up-cycle.
Cash $109.8M + marketable securities $235.9M - debt $11.6M at 2026-06-27, / 79.6M diluted shares.
Q2 annualized ~$210M; scaled by ~+40% for revenue growth to ~$1.25B and operating leverage, ~ non-GAAP net income (~$310M) less growth capex (Livermore expansion).
Equivalent to ~36x FCF, consistent with the 32x two-year-forward P/E above and with high-growth test-interface peers' trading levels.

bear.story: Memory capex and HBM test spending pause in 2027 (as the market feared in the Jul-2026 Technoprobe sell-off), Nvidia second-source ramp slips, multiple compresses to ~20x on ~$3.9 EPS.

base.story: EPS grows to ~$3.9 in 2027 with 2028E ~$4.4; multiple drifts down from ~46x trailing to ~33x forward as growth decelerates; stock roughly flat.

bull.story: HBM4/HBM4E and Nvidia GPU probe-card share ramps faster (DB: ~$200M GPU and ~$400M HBM sales by 2028), CPO systems add, EPS heads to $5.5+ in 2028 and the market keeps a 40x+ AI-test multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$80 the stock would trade near 20x 2027E EPS, a level that most likely means the AI/HBM test up-cycle has turned (a cut to the quarterly guide, a lost HBM customer or a failed Nvidia ramp), not ordinary volatility, given that the stock was still ~$96 in early September 2026.

key_uncertainties: Duration of the memory/HBM capex cycle into 2027-28 (peer Technoprobe fell 25% in mid-2026 on fears the acceleration was over).
Customer concentration: SK hynix ~30% and Nvidia >10% of revenue in Q1 2026.
Size and timing of the Nvidia GPU probe-card second-source ramp (reported by one sell-side initiation; not confirmed by the company).
Valuation: ~46x 2026E non-GAAP EPS leaves little room for a guide miss.
HBM share: DB assumes FORM loses ~40% HBM share to competitors yet still grows.
reasoning: Why the Sept 30 jump: the ~10% move from $136.25 to ~$149 coincided with Deutsche Bank initiating at Buy with a $200 target, citing FORM as second-source probe-card supplier for Nvidia GPUs at TSMC with first sales in H2 2026 and ~20% share by 2028 (>$200M sales) [2,3]. EDGAR shows no FormFactor 8-K or press release that day [12], so it was a sell-side catalyst, not company news. The Nvidia link is partly corroborated by an independent column noting Nvidia became a >10% customer in Q1 2026 [4]. Fundamentals: Q2 revenue $258.2M (+32% y/y), non-GAAP GM 53.3%, EPS $0.82, Q3 guide $270M/$0.86, net cash ~$334M [1]. Alternative signals: peer Technoprobe raised 2026 guidance after H1 revenue +42% [8] but its shares fell >25% in Jun-Jul on 'end of AI capex acceleration' fears [9], which is a reminder of how fast this group de-rates. TrendForce/Invezz see tight HBM supply and higher HBM4 pricing into 2027 [10,11]. CEO sales look like routine monthly 10b5-1-style sales of ~16-17k shares out of ~470k held, with no buying [13,14], so neutral. Job listings show continued technician/assembler hiring at Livermore/Beaverton, i.e. capacity still being added [15]. The stock swung between ~$96 (Sep 3) and ~$160 within two months, which matches the 85% realized vol. Valuation: blended fair value ~$142 (P/E 32x 2028E $4.40 plus cash; FCF yield 2.75%), a little below spot, while the bull case (DB $200, SA $170) is plausible. Distribution: a lognormal-like mixture with median ~$144-146 (slightly below spot, reflecting fair value and the de-rating risk late in the cycle) and ~55-60% effective annual vol with a fatter tail (20% weight at 95% vol) for the cycle-turn and AI-bull regimes, giving P(>=148) = 0.48, P(>=89) = 0.79 and P(>=259) = 0.17. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimates were unavailable (plan or rate limits), X/Reddit gave no usable posts (search results were spam), and Q2 call highlights came only from search summaries. Note: the brief gives a last close of $147.90, while the caller reports $149.15 for 2026-10-02; the ladders use ~$148-148.5 as the reference.
